sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name the type of immunity: (a) transfer of IgG from mother to foetus (b) vaccination with BCG.
questions.answer: (a) Passive immunity. (b) Active acquired immunity.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) B-cells mature in the thymus. (b) Memory cells give a quick response to a second exposure to an antigen.
questions.answer: (a) False – in bone marrow. (b) True.

questions.q: Name the three types of T-cells.
questions.answer: Helper T-cells (TH), cytotoxic T-cells (TC) and suppressor T-cells (TS).

questions.q: Match: (a) Plasma cells (b) Cytotoxic T-cells (c) Macrophages with (i) antibodies (ii) phagocytosis (iii) kill infected cells.
Expand: (a) BCG (b) MMR.
questions.answer: (a) Bacillus Calmette-Guerin. (b) Measles, Mumps and Rubella.

questions.q: Name two live attenuated vaccines and two killed vaccines.
questions.answer: Live: BCG and measles; killed: typhoid and rabies.

questions.q: Name the two types of specific immune responses.
questions.answer: Cell-mediated and humoral (antibody-mediated).

questions.q: Name two primary and two secondary lymphoid organs.
questions.answer: Primary: thymus and bone marrow; secondary: spleen and lymph nodes.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is meant by 'self' and 'non-self'?
questions.answer: Self is the body's own tissues; non-self is foreign material such as pathogens that the immune system recognises and attacks.

questions.q: Differentiate between B-cells and T-cells (two points).
questions.answer: B-cells mature in the bone marrow and produce antibodies (humoral); T-cells mature in the thymus and mediate cell-mediated immunity.

questions.q: What is an antigen? Name its parts which contact the antibody.
questions.answer: A foreign molecule that triggers a specific immune response; the epitope is the part that contacts the antibody paratope.

questions.q: What is the complement system?
questions.answer: A group of at least 20 plasma proteins that kill microbes without phagocytosis and help phagocytosis (opsonins).

questions.q: What are memory cells?
questions.answer: B-cells that do not become plasma cells and remain to produce antibodies quickly if the antigen appears again.

questions.q: State the difference between active and passive immunity.
questions.answer: Active: the body produces its own antibodies after infection or vaccination, long lasting; passive: ready-made antibodies are received, short-lived.

questions.q: What is a toxoid?
questions.answer: A chemically or physically modified toxin which is no longer harmful but remains immunogenic, used in vaccines against diphtheria and tetanus.

questions.q: Write any two physical barriers of innate immunity.
questions.answer: The keratinised skin with acidic secretions and the mucus with cilia in the respiratory tract.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the structure of an antibody.
questions.answer: A Y-shaped immunoglobulin with two heavy and two light chains joined by disulphide bonds; the stem (Fc) is constant while the two prongs have variable antigen-binding sites.

questions.q: Distinguish between cell-mediated and humoral immune responses (three points).
questions.answer: Cell-mediated: by T-cells, kills virus-infected and cancer cells and rejects grafts, no antibodies; humoral: by antibodies from plasma cells, acts on bacteria, toxins and free viruses.

questions.q: Describe the innate immunity and its first line of defence.
questions.answer: Physical barriers (skin, mucus, cilia, secretions), phagocytic cells and complement proteins.

questions.q: Explain the principle of vaccination.
questions.answer: Attenuated or killed germs are introduced; the body produces specific memory cells; on later exposure it responds rapidly with antibodies.

questions.q: Describe the functions of T-cells.
questions.answer: Regulate immune responses; helper T-cells activate B-cells and T-cells; cytotoxic T-cells kill infected and tumour cells; suppressor T-cells limit the response.

questions.q: Explain the classes of immunoglobulins.
questions.answer: IgG (75 per cent, crosses the placenta), IgM, IgA (in secretions and milk), IgD and IgE (allergy).

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the cells of the immune system.
questions.answer: Lymphocytes (B-cells and T-cells with their origin, maturation and functions), macrophages and plasma and memory cells.

questions.q: Explain the types of immunity with examples.
questions.answer: Innate (barriers, phagocytes, complement) and acquired (active by infection or vaccine; passive by antibodies from the mother or serum).

questions.q: Describe antigens and antibodies and the types of immune response.
questions.answer: Antigen properties and epitopes; antibody structure and classes; non-specific and specific (cell-mediated and humoral) responses.

questions.q: Describe the types of vaccines with examples, with BCG, DPT and MMR.
questions.answer: Killed, live attenuated and toxoid vaccines; BCG for TB, DPT for diphtheria, pertussis and tetanus, MMR for measles, mumps and rubella.
